num_customers: <int> Total number of customers to be served.

depot.id: <int> Identifier for the depot node in the distance matrix.
depot.x: <float> Horizontal coordinate of the depot location.
depot.y: <float> Vertical coordinate of the depot location.
depot.exogenous_time_window: <list[int], length 2> Earliest departure and latest return time for vehicles at the depot.

vehicle_capacity: <int> Maximum total demand a single vehicle can carry on one route.
num_vehicles: <str> Availability of vehicles for routing ('unlimited' means no fleet size constraint).
endogenous_time_window_width: <float> Duration of the narrow delivery time window to be assigned to each customer.

customers.id: <int> Unique identifier for the customer, corresponding to the row/column index in the distance matrix.
customers.x: <float> Horizontal coordinate of the customer location.
customers.y: <float> Vertical coordinate of the customer location.
customers.exogenous_time_window: <list[int], length 2> Earliest and latest times during which a delivery is permitted at this customer.
customers.endogenous_time_window_width: <float> Duration of the narrow delivery time window to be assigned to this customer.

scenarios.scenario_id: <int> Unique identifier for the demand scenario.
scenarios.probability: <float> Likelihood of this demand scenario occurring.
scenarios.demands: <list[int], length num_customers> Quantity of goods requested by each customer under this scenario, ordered by customer id.

distance_matrix: <list[list[float]], shape [num_customers+2][num_customers+2]> Travel cost and travel time between each pair of locations, where row/column 0 is the start depot, 1 through num_customers are customers, and num_customers+1 is the end depot.
